newsitem.title: BELGIUM: WORRIES NIBBLE AT FASTFOOD CHAIN QUICK.
newsitem.headline: WORRIES NIBBLE AT FASTFOOD CHAIN QUICK.

text.p: Shares in Belgian fastfood chain Quick lost more than two percent on the Brussels bourse, undermined by concern over Belgians' flagging appetite for its offerings and the impact that would have on cashflow.
The share was down 2.11 percent at 1,860 francs at the 1430 GMT close on a generally firmer bourse. Quick parent GIB, by contrast, was up 15 francs at 1,850.
"It is remarkable...it reflects unrest among the population about meat...less meat is being eaten in the wake of the mad cow disease story, and now there is swine fever," a trader said.

Another said there were few buyers of Quick stock. He noted the group was experiencing a slowdown in expansion and as a result cashflow was contracting, leaving less room for growth and the creation of new revenue sources.
The group was also still reeling from fallout on hamburger consumption of the mad cow disease, he said. "It takes a while for public confidence to be restored."

A third trader said Quick was losing ground on McDonald's Corp in Belgium. "It no longer has investors' interest ...the share has disappointed...1,500 (francs) would be a better price." Investors were switching from Quick to McDonald's.
